newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING DEBT MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended higher on Thursday, the long end significantly so, largely because of bund gains, dealers said.
"The longer end is certainly doing well and the curve has flattened.. We've seen some more cash in the market," one trader said.
Bunds profited from a larger than expected drop in February retail sales figures, a weaker March Ifo business climate survey and the decision by the Bundesbank to keep key rates unchanged.
The knock-on effect for bonds was most noticeable from 10 years out.
February 2007s were up 0.44 at 100.34/42 while January 2023s gained 0.71 to 113.23/43, as a number of traders bought Wednesday evening's dips.
"The Jan 06s were very well bid. One London house bought about 100 million this morning," one trader said.
The relative cheapness to bunds of January 2023s also brought out reasonable bidding in the afternoon, traders said.
Shorter maturity paper continued to underperform, the spread against bunds remaining at plus one basis point for July 6.25 percent 1998s.
A number of traders said the cheapness of short paper had encouraged some buying, but little more than a trickle.
